newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan issues policy paper on post-1997 Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan issues policy paper on post-1997 Hong Kong.

text.p: Taiwan issued a policy paper on Monday calling on arch rival China to be practical in handling Taiwan-Hong Kong ties after the territory reverts to Chinese sovereignty on July 1.

The paper, which summarises Taiwan's position towards the post-handover Hong Kong, also called "unacceptable" a proposal by communist China for Taiwan to follow Hong Kong in adopting a "one country, two systems" model for reunification.

"The Chinese communists' attempt to apply Hong Kong's one country, two systems model in handling cross-strait relations and future reunification (between Taiwan and China) is totally unacceptable to us," the paper said.
China, which would take over Hong Kong on July 1 following 156 years of British colonial rule of the colony, has vowed to allow Hong Kong to largely run itself after the handover.
But what may be considered a carrot for Hong Kong would not be enough to lure Taiwan, according to the policy paper.

"The Republic of China is a sovereignty, independent nation ... possessing its own defence capability and self-initiated diplomatic relations," Kao Koong-liang, spokesman of the cabinet's Mainland Affairs Council, read the policy paper to reporters.
"The Chinese communists' so-called 'one country, two systems' proposal basically is asking the Republic of China to surrender to the Chinese communists," the paper said.
Taiwan, whose Nationalist republic regards itself as a political equal of Beijing's communist People's Republic, split from China after the end of a civil war in 1949.

The paper said Taiwan welcomed Britain's returning of Hong Kong to the "Chinese race." Kao urged China to respect the will of Hong Kong people after the handover and abide by a promise to "let Hong Kong people rule Hong Kong," which he said would help maintain prosperity and stability in the territory.

For Taiwan's part, it would continue to strengthen its relations with, and service for, Hong Kong's people, and would continue its current economic and cultural exchanges with the territory, Kao said.
"This could create a new three-win situation for the two sides of the Taiwan Strait and Hong Kong," he said.
Kao said his council would set up a Hong Kong affairs bureau which would combine with Taiwan's current unofficial representative offices in Hong Kong.
None of Taiwan's current offices in Hong Kong carries Taiwan's official Republic of China title.
But Kao acknowledged that Taipei would tighten its control for some Hong Kong and Macau people to visit and stay in Taiwan in the post-handover period.
The Portugese enclave of Macau is scheduled to revert to Chinese sovereignty in 1999.
"Under normal conditions, there should be no special restrictions for visiting Taiwan," Kao said
"But under certain conditions, we would increase the screening of their visiting applications," he said.
He said the people who may face stricter screening are those who move from China to Hong Kong after the handover and to Macau in 1999.
